sources.entry: chromadb - An open-source embedding database for building AI applications with semantic search.

summary.one_liner: Chroma is an open-source embedding database for AI applications that stores documents, computes embeddings, and runs semantic search and metadata-filtered queries.
summary.what_it_does: Provides a Python client (pip install chromadb) and a JavaScript client (npm package chromadb) for working with collections of documents. The README's core API shows creating a collection, adding documents with optional metadata and ids, and querying for the most similar results by query text. Chroma handles tokenization, embedding, and indexing automatically by default, and users can supply their own embeddings instead. Queries can be filtered on metadata with a where clause or on document content with where_document (for example $contains). It can run in-memory for prototyping, or in client-server mode via the chroma run command with a persistence path. The README also mentions a hosted option, Chroma Cloud, for serverless vector, hybrid, and full-text search.
use_cases: building retrieval for AI or LLM applications
prototyping a vector store in memory
running a local client-server vector database
notable: Core API is four main functions: create, add, query, and get, with get_or_create and delete also available
Automatic tokenization, embedding, and indexing, with option to bring your own embeddings
Metadata and document-content filters on queries
Same project offers in-memory mode and client-server mode
Hosted Chroma Cloud service mentioned in the README
caveats: The README says the row-based API is coming soon, so that interface is not yet available
Chroma Cloud is a hosted paid service with free credits to start, as described in the README
The README does not describe scale limits or production deployment details
